title: Market complementarity and vessel-sharing alliances
x: Market complementarity between potential liner-shipping alliance partners
timeHorizon: Formation of the proposed vessel-sharing alliance
setting: Two liner-shipping firms consider forming a vessel-sharing alliance. Both must participate voluntarily. They share at least one market. Market complementarity concerns nonoverlapping market coverage and is distinct from compatibility of operating resources.
task: Rate how higher market complementarity changes the likelihood that the firms establish a vessel-sharing alliance. Compare lower X (More overlapping market portfolios) with higher X (More nonoverlapping markets, retaining at least one common market). Use the same X contrast in both contexts. A positive rating means higher X is associated with more Y; a negative rating means less Y. Rate the relationship, not the overall level of Y. Do not interpret this judgment as a measured empirical coefficient.

xContrast.higher: More nonoverlapping markets, retaining at least one common market

sharedFacts: The outcome is whether the potential vessel-sharing alliance forms, not the performance of an established alliance.
The lower-versus-higher market-complementarity contrast retains at least one common market and is identical across contexts.

sourceEvidence.citation: Mitsuhashi, H., and Greve, H. R. (2009). A Matching Theory of Alliance Formation and Organizational Success: Complementarity and Compatibility. Academy of Management Journal, 52(5), 975-995.
sourceEvidence.measurementNotes: Global liner shipping; market definitions and resource compatibility held constant
sourceEvidence.translationNotes: Index is symmetric difference divided by union, but zero when no common market. Economic values are unweighted. Matching requires mutual participation.
